title: I spent 3 weeks rebuilding our RAG chunking pipeline from scratch. Here is what actually happened.
body:
I built our team's first semantic chunking system three weeks ago, convinced it would solve our retrieval hallucination problem.

Instead, latency jumped 4x and our vector database bill doubled overnight.

Here is the raw architectural post-mortem and the 3 decisions that finally dropped retrieval errors by 68%:

1. Fixed vs Semantic Chunking:
We thought semantic chunking based on sentence embeddings was the holy grail. But chunk boundary drift caused related functions to get sliced in half. We reverted to recursive character chunking (800 token target, 150 token overlap) with document hierarchy metadata prepended to each chunk.

2. The Embedding Bottleneck:
Calling OpenAI text-embedding-3-small on 500k chunks dynamically on ingest was burning 42 minutes per index run. Moving to local bge-small-en-v1.5 running on ONNX runtime sliced indexing time to 4.2 minutes.

3. Reranking is 80% of the game:
Vector similarity alone retrieved superficially similar docstrings. Adding Cohere rerank-v3 as a secondary pass across top 25 candidates gave us the true quality jump.

Have you tested hybrid search vs pure vector similarity in your production agents? What chunking size gave you the highest recall?

title: I shipped our first multi-agent workflow into production. 48 hours later, it caught fire.
body:
I made the classic mistake of giving autonomous agents open-ended tool loops without cycle budgets.

At 2:14 AM on Tuesday, two agents entered an infinite critique loop debate over JSON formatting. $380 in API tokens burned before our circuit breaker tripped.

Here are the 4 strict safety constraints we implemented before turning it back on:

1. Deterministic state machines over autonomous agent swarms. LangGraph or strict DAGs beat freeform ReAct loops every single time in production.
2. Hard token and iteration budgets per execution context (max 3 tool retries).
3. Pydantic validation at tool interfaces instead of asking the model 'did that look right?'.
4. Idempotency keys on all state mutation tools.

If you are building AI agents today, never let two LLMs talk to each other without a deterministic arbiter in the middle.

title: Why did we rewrite our background worker queue from Celery to native Python asyncio?
body:
I replaced our Redis + Celery worker cluster with a lightweight async Python engine, and everyone thought I was crazy.

We were paying $600/month for worker dynos that spent 92% of their CPU cycles idling on HTTP timeouts to external LLM APIs.

Here is how we redesigned it:

```python
async def process_batch(items: list[Job]):
    async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
        tasks = [tg.create_task(run_pipeline(job)) for job in items]
    return [t.result() for t in tasks]
```

By leveraging `asyncio.TaskGroup` with semaphore concurrency throttles, a single 1GB container handled 1,200 concurrent webhook streams without breaking a sweat.

title: I tried 7 different LLM caching strategies so you don't have to.
body:
I built a benchmark testing exact matching, Redis semantic vector caching, prompt prefix caching, and client-side sqlite caches.

Here is the real data across 100,000 production requests:

- Semantic vector caching had a 24% false-positive match rate where subtle nuances in user prompts returned completely wrong answers.
- Prompt prefix caching (supported natively by Anthropic and Gemini) reduced latency by 64% with 0% accuracy penalty.
- Exact SHA-256 prompt hashing cached 38% of identical system queries for practically zero engineering overhead.

Conclusion: Start with deterministic prefix caching and exact hashes before reaching for complex semantic vector caches.

title: I shipped an AI feature without user telemetry. Big mistake.
body:
I launched our 'Smart Summary' feature with high hopes and celebratory team Slack messages.

Two weeks later, we finally wired up PostHog telemetry.

The retention rate was 4%. Only 12 out of 300 active users clicked the summary button more than once.

Why? Because summary generation took 8 seconds with no streaming feedback. Users thought the app was frozen and navigated away.

We added server-sent events (SSE) streaming and immediate optimistic loading indicators. Usage jumped 5.4x in 4 days. Perception of speed matters more than raw speed.

title: I replaced LangChain with 150 lines of pure Python. Here is the exact diff.
body:
I spent an entire weekend debugging an obscure LCEL runnable chaining traceback that led into 14 nested framework abstractions.

I deleted `langchain`, `langchain-community`, and `langchain-core` from our pyproject.toml.

Here is what replaced it:
- Direct `httpx.AsyncClient` calls with tenacity retries.
- Native Pydantic `model_validate_json()`.
- Simple python dictionary prompts with `.format()`.

Our Docker image size dropped from 1.8GB to 140MB. Cold boot times dropped from 6.8s to 420ms. Most importantly, junior engineers on our team could actually read and debug the code without opening framework documentation.

Keep your AI plumbing thin and explicit.

title: Implementing Server-Sent Events (SSE) in FastAPI with real-time UI indicators
body:
Here is how to stream generation stage updates to React using FastAPI's StreamingResponse.

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
import asyncio, json

app = FastAPI()

async def event_generator():
    for stage in ['strategy', 'drafting', 'review']:
        data = json.dumps({'stage': stage, 'status': 'running'})
        yield f'event: stage\ndata: {data}\n\n'
        await asyncio.sleep(1)
```

Key details to keep in mind:
- Ensure nginx or your reverse proxy has proxy_buffering turned off.
- Handle client disconnects using `request.is_disconnected()`.
- Always send keepalive pings every 15 seconds to prevent NAT gateway timeouts.

Database indexing strategies for PostgreSQL JSONB columns in production
body:
When storing unstructured metadata or LLM run logs in PostgreSQL JSONB fields, table scans will degrade query speed exponentially as rows grow.

Create a GIN index on top-level keys:
```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_runs_metadata ON generation_runs USING GIN (strategy_json);
```

Or for specific path queries:
```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_opportunity_score ON generation_runs (((strategy_json->>'opportunity_score')::int));
```

This drops filter latencies from 320ms to 4ms on tables with over 500k records.

title: Optimizing SQLite for async Python web applications
body:
SQLite is capable of handling remarkable read and write throughput if configured properly on startup:

- Enable Write-Ahead Logging (WAL mode): `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;`
- Set busy timeout so concurrent writers wait instead of throwing immediate lock errors: `PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000;`
- Increase cache size: `PRAGMA cache_size=-64000;` (64MB RAM cache)
- Set synchronous to NORMAL: `PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL;`

With these four pragmas, SQLite can easily handle hundreds of queries per second with aiosqlite.

title: What is Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)? A high level overview
body:
Have you wondered how LLMs access private organizational data? The answer is RAG.

RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation. It combines information retrieval with text generation.

The process works in three basic steps:
1. Ingestion: Documents are converted into vector embeddings.
2. Retrieval: Relevant passages are fetched based on semantic similarity.
3. Generation: The LLM answers the prompt using retrieved passages as context.

RAG helps reduce hallucinations and ensures up-to-date knowledge.

title: Understanding Vector Databases: What are embeddings and cosine distance?
body:
Vector databases have gained immense popularity recently. But how do they work?

Embeddings represent textual or multimodal data as arrays of floating-point numbers in high-dimensional space.

Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors to determine their semantic relationship.

Popular vector databases include Pinecone, Qdrant, Chroma, and pgvector. They are essential for modern AI applications.

title: What is Docker and containerization? A guide for beginners
body:
Containerization has revolutionized modern software development.

Docker allows developers to package applications along with their dependencies into lightweight, standalone containers.

Benefits of containers:
- Portability across environments
- Consistency between dev and prod

Getting started with Docker is an essential skill for any software engineer today.

title: Introduction to Prompt Engineering for developers
body:
Prompt engineering is the practice of structuring text that can be interpreted and understood by generative AI models.

Best practices include:
- Being clear and specific
- Providing few-shot examples
- Specifying the desired output format
- Assigning a persona or role

Mastering prompt design helps you get better results from ChatGPT and Claude.

title: What is Serverless Computing? Pros and cons explained
body:
Serverless architectures allow you to build and run applications without thinking about servers.

Pros:
- No server management
- Automatic scaling
- Pay only for compute time used

Cons:
- Cold starts
- Vendor lock-in
- Debugging complexity

It is great for event-driven workflows and APIs.

title: Why full-stack engineers are replacing specialized teams in early stage startups
body:
The era of having a separate frontend engineer, backend engineer, and QA engineer for every small product feature is fading.

With modern frameworks like Next.js, FastAPI, and AI-assisted IDEs, a single full-stack engineer can ship an entire verified feature from database schema to responsive UI in 48 hours.

Coordination overhead between siloed roles kills velocity faster than technical debt ever will.

What matters most today is end-to-end product intuition and ownership.

title: The most underrated skill for senior engineers is technical writing
body:
You can write the most elegant distributed consensus algorithm in the world.

If you cannot explain why it matters in a 1-page design doc that executives and peers can understand, your architecture will get rejected or ignored.

Code proves you can solve a problem. Writing proves you understand which problem is worth solving in the first place.

Invest in writing clearly. It has a higher ROI than learning your 5th JavaScript framework.
